biological.summary: Overexpression of TCF4 in umbilical cord blood cells resulted in a twofold increase in erythroid colony forming units (CFU-Es), while knockdown caused a dramatic decrease in erythroid colonies. TCF4 knockdown and overexpression both inhibited megakaryocyte colony formation, but had no impact on granulocyte or macrophage colonies. In MDS patients, TCF4 mRNA expression was lower in hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors, and MEPs compared to healthy controls, correlating with lower hemoglobin levels.

biological.citation: Suppression of TCF4 promotes a ZC3H12A-mediated self-sustaining inflammatory feedback cycle involving IL-17RA/IL-17RE epidermal signaling (PMID: 38470486)
biological.summary: siRNA knockdown of TCF4 in human keratinocytes increased IL17C expression, and IL-17C stimulation decreased TCF4 while increasing NFKBIZ and ZC3H12A in an IL-17RA/RE-dependent manner, creating a proinflammatory feedback loop. In the KC-Tie2 inflammatory dermatitis mouse model, TCF4 protein was decreased in lesional skin concomitant with increases in IL-17C and Zc3h12a, which reversed upon genetic elimination of Il17c, Il17ra, and Il17re. Interference with Tcf4 in KC-Tie2 mouse skin increased Il17c and exacerbated the inflammatory skin phenotype, identifying TCF4 as a negative regulator of IL-17C-driven skin inflammation.

biological.citation: Transcription Factor 4 loss-of-function is associated with deficits in progenitor proliferation and cortical neuron content (PMID: 35501322)
biological.summary: Neural progenitor cells and brain organoids derived from Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome patients with TCF4 mutations showed reduced proliferation, impaired neuronal differentiation, reduced cortical neuron content, and impaired electrical activity. TCF4 loss-of-function led to decreased Wnt signaling and diminished expression of SOX genes, culminating in reduced progenitor proliferation in vitro. These phenotypes were rescued by correction of TCF4 expression or pharmacological modulation of Wnt signaling.

biological.citation: Deciphering novel TCF4-driven mechanisms underlying a common triplet repeat expansion-mediated disease (PMID: 38713708)
biological.summary: Long-read, short-read, and spatial transcriptomic analyses of primary patient-derived corneal endothelial cells revealed global altered splicing and TCF4 isoform ratio skewing specifically in CTG18.1-expanded FECD cases. Differential gene expression and exon usage analyses identified expansion-specific transcriptomic biomarkers, supporting both RNA toxicity and TCF4 isoform-specific dysregulation as pathogenic mechanisms. Exome data from 134 CTG18.1-independent FECD cases identified rare, potentially deleterious TCF4 variants in 7/134 cases, suggesting TCF4 variants independent of the repeat expansion also increase FECD risk.
biological.sample_size: 134 Exp- FECD cases; large cohort of Exp+ and Exp- FECD patients

biological.citation: Transcriptional regulation of daily sleep amount by TCF4-HDAC4-CREB complex in mice (PMID: 39745887)
biological.summary: AAV-mediated expression of TCF4 (and related class I bHLH factors TCF3, TCF12) across mouse brain neurons reduced both REM and non-REM sleep duration. TCF4 requires its bHLH domain to regulate sleep amount, and physically interacts with CREB and HDAC4 via this domain to cooperatively regulate daily sleep. The ability of CREB to regulate sleep duration also requires its binding to TCF4 and HDAC4, placing TCF4 in a transcriptional complex controlling sleep.

biological.citation: TCF4 Promotes Neuroblastoma Proliferation and Inhibits Ferroptosis by Transactivating GPX4 Expression (PMID: 40668527)
biological.summary: TCF4 mRNA and protein were significantly upregulated in neuroblastoma tissues and cell lines. TCF4 knockdown reduced proliferation, elevated ROS accumulation and lipid peroxidation, and altered iron metabolism markers (FTH1, TFR1). ChIP and dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed direct TCF4 occupancy and transcriptional activation of GPX4 promoter, and GPX4 overexpression rescued the anti-proliferative and pro-ferroptotic effects of TCF4 knockdown.

TCF4 is described as a master regulator that drives downstream transcriptional programs in blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN), and its activity is dependent on the BET protein BRD4. TCF4 expression is a highly sensitive diagnostic marker for BPDCN, augmenting diagnostic specificity alongside CD4, CD56, CD123, and TCL1. BRD4 inhibition provides a therapeutic vulnerability by disrupting TCF4-driven transcriptional programs in this malignancy.

A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identified a SNP in intron 4 of TCF4 associated with schizophrenia. TCF4 encodes a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that interacts with other transcription factors to activate or repress gene expression, and haploinsufficiency causes Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome. The review proposes that TCF4, NRXN1, and CNTNAP2 may participate in a shared biological pathway altered in schizophrenia and other neuropsychiatric disorders.

biological.citation: Tcf4 Deficiency causes recurrent seizures in mice (PMID: 40619119)
biological.summary: Mice with heterozygous deletion of Tcf4 in Aldh1l1-expressing cells (astrocytes and other cell types) developed astrogliosis by postnatal day 4, severe recurrent seizures beginning at three months, and shortened lifespans—the first PTHS mouse model to exhibit seizures. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed widespread gene expression changes in excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes, including genes associated with epilepsy. Increased neuronal activity was observed in cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, and hypothalamus, demonstrating a critical role for TCF4 in astrocyte-dependent CNS homeostasis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Convergence of genes and pathways influencing neurodevelopment following suppression of ASD-associated chromatin modifiers and transcriptional regulators in human neural progenitor cells (ASHG 2015)
biological.summary: RNAi-mediated suppression of TCF4 in iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs) revealed strong overlap between genes regulated by TCF4 and those regulated by CHD8, converging on cell adhesion and Wnt/Notch signaling subnetworks enriched for ASD-associated genes. The transcriptional consequences of TCF4 loss-of-function in NPCs were significantly correlated with co-expression modules influencing developmental timing in the brain. These findings indicate that highly penetrant TCF4 loss-of-function mutations associated with Pitt-Hopkins syndrome and ASD converge on shared early neurodevelopmental pathways.
